newsitem.title: TUNISIA: IBM opens North Africa-Malta HQ in Tunis.
newsitem.headline: IBM opens North Africa-Malta HQ in Tunis.

text.p: IBM announced on Thursday the establishment in Tunis of its headquarters for five North African countries and Malta where it had combined turnover of about $100 million last year.
Christian Poujardieu, General Manager of IBM North Africa, told a press conference that the new structure will cover Algeria, Egypt, Malta, Morocco, Mauritania and Tunisia.

Studies conducted by IBM in 1995 showed that there was a potential of growth in African emerging markets, provided IBM reinforced its presence and invested there for the medium and long term, he said.
The market is expected to grow at an average 12 percent a year, IBM officials said.

IBM is the leader in the Tunisian computers market where its turnover in 1995 amounted to 15.5 million dinars ($15.82 million), Tarek Zarg el Ayoun, general manager of Tunisian Business Machines (TBM), a subsidiary 70-percent-owned by IBM-France in Tunis said.
He said that based on Tunisian official statistics, TBM has an 11.5 percent share in Tunisia's computer imports. ($1=0.98 dinar) -- Tunis newsroom, 2161-787538
